title: Integrated Socio‐Economic and Drinking Water Quality Analysis
content:
ABSTRACT

Access to clean drinking water is vital for health, but water pollution remains a global concern, causing millions of deaths annually. Traditional methods for assessing water quality struggle to address the complex and interconnected factors influencing water pollution. Recent studies have advanced water quality prediction through AI, but many have lacked standardized frameworks and failed to incorporate socio-economic factors. This study introduces a novel hybrid PSO and ANN model to address these limitations. It evaluates regional water availability, infrastructure coverage, mean water supply levels, dependency ratio, per capita water availability and water quality indicators such as pH, TDS, EC, Chlorides, Nitrates, Sulphates and Hardness. Sensitivity analysis identified pH and Nitrates as the most influential parameters, while socio-economic indicators like dependency ratio and mean water supply also contributed significantly. The findings highlight disparities in water availability, infrastructure gaps and contamination risks. The model offers a scalable solution for water quality assessment.
